customer_question: Several OPP profile test cases failed and the cause isn't clear from our test logs - how should we proceed?
question_variants: OPP profile test cases keep failing - how should we proceed?
Do we need the customer's input on how to operate the test sample for OPP tests?
What should be sent to the customer when OPP test cases fail?
actual_issue: Multiple OPP (Object Push Profile) test cases (OPP/SR/GOEP/SRM, SRMP, BCE, BCP, GOEP/BC) resulted in FAIL when executed according to the customer's procedure document. The cause was not clear from the test execution alone.
plain_english_explanation: When Profile test cases fail and the cause isn't obvious from the test logs, the testing lab may need to send the failure logs (a PTS report with logs, plus terminal/TeraTerm logs showing the test execution) to the customer/device manufacturer and ask for guidance on how to properly operate the test sample (DUT) for that specific test case - since the manufacturer knows their device's UI/behavior best.
consultant_answer: Please send the customer the PTS report with logs and the TeraTerm logs for the failing OPP test cases, and ask for advice on how to operate the test sample for these tests.
decision_logic: When Profile test case failures can't be resolved through the standard test procedure and the root cause appears related to how the test sample (DUT) needs to be operated, send the relevant PTS log report and execution logs (e.g., TeraTerm) to the customer/manufacturer and request operational guidance for those specific test cases.
final_recommendation: For unresolved OPP (or similar) profile test failures, escalate to the customer with the PTS report and execution logs attached, requesting guidance on correct test sample operation for the failing test cases.
risk_if_done_wrong: Repeatedly re-running failing test cases without manufacturer input on correct DUT operation could waste testing time without resolving the failures, and could result in test cases remaining incorrectly marked FAIL in the final report due to operator error rather than an actual device defect.
